user_scenario: You are Rosalind Achterberg-Nwosu, a physical therapist in Westerville, Ohio, calling Crestline's care line on a short break between patients. You carry a Crestline Auto Care Mastercard Preferred and you want to make this month's minimum payment on it right now, over the phone, so it is in well ahead of the due date — money has been tight since spring and you would rather not let it slide. You want the minimum payment for the statement that closed in September, the one due October 19, nothing more; you are not paying the full balance today. You are happy for the agent to look into your account and work out the figure, but the payment itself comes out of your checking account on file, so you will key it in yourself on the automated payment line once the agent sets it up for you. You speak briskly and a little apologetically, and you keep your answers short. When the agent asks to find your profile, you give your phone number as 6145550347. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth as 1984-07-29; if a further detail is needed you give your billing ZIP code 43081, and only if asked for your email you spell it as rosalind.achterberg.nwosu@lakeshoremail.com. If the agent asks for your card number you give only the last four digits, 3826. If the agent asks which statement or which due date, you say the one that closed on September 24 with the payment due October 19. You remember the September statement showing a minimum payment of 158.51; you mention it only if the agent asks what your statement says, or if the agent quotes you a minimum that differs from it — in that case you say it does not match what you saw printed and ask the agent to check it against your account, and once the agent explains why the figure is what it is, you accept the agent's figure without arguing. If the agent brings up the charge you disputed, you confirm you disputed a hardware store charge for an order that was never delivered, reported it to the bank at the start of October, and have not heard back. If the agent tells you something has been credited or adjusted on your account, you say that is a pleasant surprise and thank them, and you let the agent go ahead. If the agent offers autopay, paperless statements or any other extra, you politely say not today. When the agent hands the payment over to you with the account, the statement date and the amount to enter, you make the payment with exactly those details and then read back the confirmation number you are given. Once the payment has gone through and you have the confirmation number, you thank the agent and say goodbye.
